change_vs_ref: + --aug_opus_plc_p 0.3 (in-process libopus round trip with Gilbert-Elliott loss and decoder PLC on 30% of codec calls; --aug_opus_loss 0.01 0.20 and --aug_opus_burst 1 4 left at default)
rationale:
This is the pre-registered iteration b of the B4 screen. wave.json lever_notes say "iterations a-c are the queued arms in this order, apm_ns -> opus_plc -> dtx_gate, each exactly its `set` on top of B2f's argv". plan_snapshot.md row b is `opus_plc` `--aug_opus_plc_p 0.3`. The B4a analyst re-ranked its proposals with opus_plc first (analyze.result.json rank 1). user_notes.md has no steering notes, so the queue order applies. Base = B2f, because new_best_delta 100 keeps B2f as the reference for the whole wave; B4a's verdict was "drop" on both readouts (exploop/B4/iter01/verdict.json), so its flag is not carried over.

Evidence. The largest remaining error in the B4a report (docs/experiments-exploration/b4-experiments/20261018_194212_B4a_...md) is still noisy heldout bona: B2f sim_heldout_v1 F1 87.92 / 88.27 (merge / final) with R_bona 69.31 / 69.82 against R_spoof 99.00 / 99.13 (report section 2.2). The report also found that B4a raised online heldout spoof misses on half B (5 -> 11 merge, 4 -> 9 final) and pushed the PLC spoof-miss guard from 16 -> 23 (bound 26). opus_plc targets that slice directly. It is the only B4 lever that changes the codec slot: online sources plus concealment of dropped packets, which B2f never trained on. B2f online PLC-treated vs untreated heldout bona recall is 67.5 / 75.6, G +0.95 (b4_dsp_slices.py via the report, section 7). The apm_ns mechanism was refuted (NS DiD +0.49 > refute line +0.32), so the next step is a different mechanism, not a higher NS dose; analyst proposals 3-4 (apm_ns dose / levels) stay as candidates for iteration d.

Constraints. One factor: `--aug_opus_plc_p` is in the coupled group [--aug_opus_plc_p, --aug_opus_loss, --aug_opus_burst], and the loss and burst ranges stay at the trainer defaults (0.01..0.20, 1..4) as the plan specifies. The flag is in `allowed`. Nothing forbidden is touched. The fixed flags are unchanged, num_epochs stays 8 (max 10) and batch_size stays 16 per the plan. Trainer preconditions (b4wave/augment.py _init_opus_plc): it needs the codec stage (`--use_rtc_aug`, present) and `--aug_codec_profiles fixed` (the default; the B4a stdout shows `Codec profiles: fixed`). Both hold on the B2f argv. No derived values are needed. The plan pre-registers a zero-loss attribution control (`--aug_opus_plc_p 0.3 --aug_opus_loss 0 0`) for iteration d if this arm is positive on the WF1 CI rule.
hypothesis: Concealment artefacts are read as synthesis. B2f never trained on a dropped packet. Online heldout bona that went through packet-loss concealment trails untreated online bona (recall 67.5 vs 75.6, logit gap +0.95, per the B4a report section 7 and the wave.json lever_queue). On 30% of codec calls, B4b replaces the ffmpeg codec with an in-process libopus round trip using the same app/bitrate/cutoff/frame draws, Gilbert-Elliott bursty loss (target PLR 1-20%, mean burst 1-4 packets) and decoder PLC, on both classes. This should make concealment class-neutral, so heldout bona false alarms on the PLC slice drop and heldout F1 rises. The local premise is weak: the typical null-panel PLC gap is smaller (panel mu -0.57, sd 0.41 on DiD), and B4a, which never saw packet loss, already reached online-PLC DiD -0.50 (final) / -0.61 (merge). So this arm is mainly a pre-registered outcome test of ADD-C's PLC result in the RTC setting, with the mechanism capped at 'directional'.
predicted_signature: Mechanism (scripts/b4_dsp_slices.py --lever opus_plc, --ref = B2f's same readout, --placebo = B4a; full sets): online PLC-vs-no-PLC bona DiD < -0.57 (panel mu) on the final readout and below B4a's -0.50 (final) / -0.61 (merge), so it is at least 'directional'. 'Shown' (DiD <= -1.39) is not claimed. Report the offline PLC contrast and bona logit/recall by realised-loss bin. Outcome: sim_heldout_v1 F1 up >= 0.5 from 87.92 / 88.27 (merge / final), driven by R_bona rising from 69.31 / 69.82 with R_spoof near 99.00 / 99.13. Expected half_B WF1 delta vs B2f 0 to +0.4 (lever_queue) against 91.98 / 92.14. Must not move: dev_online_clean F1 within 0.5 of 97.60 / 97.69; sim_matched_v1 F1 down <= 0.5 from 91.22 / 91.24; matched qq and wechat bona recall each down <= 6 from 61.62 / 71.15; full-set PLC spoof misses <= 26 / 25 (B2f 16 / 15); online heldout spoof misses not above B4a's 11 / 9 on half B; ep1 TrainAcc within 2 of 87.36. Train log: 'Epoch N B3 aug' / 'B4 aug-by-class' lines show opus_plc counts near 0.3 x 75,785 codec calls, balanced across classes, with the plc_l0_5 / plc_l5_10 / plc_l10p bins populated and fail_opus_plc near 0.
falsifier: (1) Mechanism refuted: online PLC DiD >= -0.57 (DiD* >= 0, no better than an average null retrain) AND heldout F1 delta < +0.5 on either readout: libopus PLC exposure does not carry over to heldout concealment. Drop. (2) half_B WF1 delta < -0.5 (below the ±0.5 band) with the shared under-fit signature (ep1 TrainAcc < 85.36 or ep8 TrainLoss > 0.0752): a B3d-type codec-side under-fit. Drop. (3) Guard break: full-set PLC spoof misses > 26 (merge) / > 25 (final), matched qq or wechat bona recall down > 6, or clean F1 down > 0.5: concealment became a bona cue, or matched codec fidelity was lost. Drop. (4) A high fail_opus_plc count in the train log: the arm was not dosed as designed (confounded, not refuted). Wave verdict rule: positive = merge half_B WF1 delta > +0.5 with CI low > 0 and clean drop <= 0.5. If positive, iteration d runs the zero-loss control `--aug_opus_plc_p 0.3 --aug_opus_loss 0 0`; if that control gives >= half the WF1 gain, the gain goes to the decoder path, not to PLC.
eval_note: Screen arm: B2f stays the reference (new_best_delta 100). Compare both readouts (merge_top5, epoch_8) with B2f-top5 / B2f-ep8 on the 17 sls_local17 sets with a 2000-sample bootstrap CI. Run scripts/b4_dsp_slices.py --lever opus_plc on merge and final with --ref = B2f's same readout and --placebo = B4a's readout (B4a is now the first placebo arm: its PLC_online DiD is -0.50 final / -0.61 merge, so opus_plc must go below those). Also report the NS and VAD contrasts of this arm, because B4b is a placebo for apm_ns and dtx_gate at the wave SUMMARY. Watch sim_heldout_v1 R_bona (online/PLC slices), the PLC and online heldout spoof misses, matched qq/wechat bona recall, dev_online_clean F1, and fail_opus_plc / plc-bin counts in train.log.
header_text: B4b = B2f + --aug_opus_plc_p 0.3 (opus_plc arm, iteration b of the B4 screen; rdloop B4 module b4wave). On 30% of codec calls (separate B4 RNG stream), the ffmpeg codec is replaced by an in-process libopus 1.3.1 round trip with the same app/bitrate/cutoff/frame draws, Gilbert-Elliott bursty packet loss (target loss 0.01..0.20, mean burst 1..4 packets; defaults of the coupled flags) and decoder packet-loss concealment at 48 kHz, on both classes. Target: B2f's weakest set, sim_heldout_v1: F1 87.92 / 88.27 (merge / final) with R_bona 69.31 / 69.82 against R_spoof 99.00 / 99.13 (B4a report section 2.2). In it, PLC-treated online bona trails untreated online bona: recall 67.5 vs 75.6, G +0.95 (B4a report section 7). B4a raised online heldout spoof misses (half B 5 -> 11 / 4 -> 9), and this arm also tests whether loss-concealment exposure fixes that slice. The mechanism is capped at 'directional'; the arm is an outcome test of ADD-C's PLC result. B4a (apm_ns, verdict drop) is the placebo arm for the PLC contrast. Everything else is B2f's argv, 8 epochs, batch 16, seed 1234.
